mainTopic: Intent for ערלים at the זריקה of the קרבן פסח: רב חסדא and רבה, their competing readings of a ברייתא on ״וכל ערל״ and ״זאת״, and רב אשי's objection
overview: Someone slaughters the קרבן פסח for circumcised people, but intends that uncircumcised people (ערלים) get atonement through the sprinkling (זריקה) of its blood. רב חסדא says the offering is פסול, and רבה says it is כשר. The argument is whether intent for ערלים counts at the זריקה or only at the שחיטה. רבה brings a ברייתא that asks whether one ערל ruins the פסח for the whole group. The ברייתא tries comparing ערלה to טומאה and then to זמן, and each comparison can be countered, so it decides through the verse ״זאת״. In רבה's reading, ״וכל ערל״ teaches that only a fully ערל group disqualifies, and ״זאת״ limits even that to שחיטה, because intent about the eaters has no effect at זריקה. רב חסדא reads the ברייתא the opposite way: at זריקה even a partly ערל group disqualifies, because פיגול is fixed only at the זריקה. רב אשי rejects both readings, since ״וכל ערל״ might mean 'any ערל', and he begins his own explanation of the dispute, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case: slaughtered for circumcised people, sprinkled with ערלים in mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presents a new case and the dispute between רב חסדא (פסול) and רבה (כשר).
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughtered the פסח for circumcised people, on condition that uncircumcised people get atonement through the sprinkling, רב חסדא said: it is disqualified. רבה said: it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a case. The שחיטה was done properly, for circumcised people. But the person intended that ערלים should be atoned for through the זריקה. Two אמוראים argue about whether this ruins the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wrong intent for ערלים at the שחיטה is already known to disqualify a פסח. The new question is whether that same kind of intent also matters when it happens only at the זריקה stage. רב חסדא says the offering is פסול, and רבה says it is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: uncircumcised people, who may not eat the פסח
sprinkling of the blood on the altar
on condition / with the intent that

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it for circumcised people,
on condition that there would be atonement through it
for uncircumcised people, through the sprinkling.
Rav Chisda said: it is disqualified.
Rabba said: it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחָטוֹ לְמוּלִין, עַל מְנָת שֶׁיִּתְכַּפְּרוּ בּוֹ עֲרֵלִים בִּזְרִיקָה

steps.title: The reasoning behind each opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the principle behind each side: does intent for ערלים work at the זריקה or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said it is disqualified: intent for ערלים counts at the sprinkling. רבה said it is valid: intent for ערלים does not count at the sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the root of the argument. The question is whether the rule of מחשבת ערלים applies at the זריקה, or only at the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that intent for ערלים at the שחיטה ruins the פסח. רב חסדא extends this to the זריקה. רבה limits it to the שחיטה, so in our case, where the שחיטה was proper, the offering stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: intent that the offering be for uncircumcised people
there is not (it does not apply)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבה permits ערלים to eat or take part in the פסח. He only says that a wrong thought at the זריקה stage does not ruin an offering that was slaughtered properly.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said it is disqualified —
intent for uncircumcised people applies at the sprinkling.
Rabba said it is valid —
intent for uncircumcised people does not apply at the sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר פָּסוּל — יֵשׁ מַחְשֶׁבֶת עֲרֵלִים בִּזְרִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the principle behind the two rulings in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא: יש מחשבת ערלים בזריקה. רבה: אין מחשבת ערלים בזריקה.

steps.title: רבה brings a ברייתא: does one ערל ruin it for the whole group?
steps.stepSummary: רבה says he has a source, and begins quoting a ברייתא about a group with one ערל among them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: From where do I say this? As a ברייתא teaches: You might think an uncircumcised person would disqualify the other members of the group who come with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה starts bringing a proof for his view. The ברייתא he quotes opens with a 'you might think' question: if one member of the group is a ערל, is the פסח ruined for everyone? This step is setting up the ברייתא's discussion in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about a partial problem: only some of the people the offering was slaughtered for are ערלים. It tries two competing logical comparisons and then decides through the verse ״זאת״. The גמרא's reading of that verse is what gives רבה his proof about the זריקה (step 10).

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this?
members of the group registered for the פסח

phrases.english: Rabba said: From where do I say this?
As it was taught in a baraita:
You might think he would disqualify the members of the group
who come with him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה supports his view from step 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's view: אין מחשבת ערלים בזריקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about whether one ערל in the group ruins the פסח for the rest

steps.title: First comparison: ערלה is like טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא argues by logic that a partial ערלה should not ruin the offering, just like a partial טומאה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It can be shown by logic: since ערלה disqualifies and טומאה disqualifies, then just as with טומאה, partial טומאה was not treated like full טומאה, so too with ערלה, partial ערלה is not treated like full ערלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tries to answer its own question with a logical comparison. ערלה and טומאה both disqualify a פסח. With טומאה, one impure member does not ruin the offering for everyone, so the same should be true of ערלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מקצת' here means only part of the group has the problem. With טומאה, a partial problem is not treated like a full one. The ברייתא carries that rule over to ערלה, so the other members would be fine.

keyTerms.meaning: and it is logical (a reasoned derivation)

phrases.english: And it is logical:
since lack of circumcision disqualifies
and impurity disqualifies,
just as with impurity, [the Torah] did not make
partial impurity like full impurity —
so too with lack of circumcision, it did not make
partial lack of circumcision like full lack of circumcision.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִין הוּא: הוֹאִיל וְעׇרְלָה פּוֹסֶלֶת וְטוּמְאָה פּוֹסֶלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא's first attempt to answer the question raised in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Compared to טומאה, a partial ערלה does not disqualify the whole group.

steps.title: Rival comparison: maybe ערלה is like זמן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a competing comparison to intent beyond the allowed time (זמן), where a partial problem does ruin everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way: since ערלה disqualifies and זמן disqualifies, then just as with זמן, partial זמן was treated like full זמן, so too with ערלה, partial ערלה is treated like full ערלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its first comparison by offering a different one that leads to the opposite answer. If ערלה is like זמן, then even one ערל in the group would ruin the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זמן' means intending to eat the offering after its allowed time (פיגול). There, even intent about a small part of the offering ruins it completely. If ערלה follows זמן, a partial ערלה would be treated like a full one.

keyTerms.meaning: or go this other way (a competing comparison)
intent to eat beyond the allowed time

phrases.english: Or go this way:
since lack of circumcision disqualifies
and intent beyond the time disqualifies,
just as with time — it made
partial time-intent like full time-intent,
so too with lack of circumcision — it made
partial lack of circumcision like full lack of circumcision.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an opposite comparison that challenges step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of ערלה to טומאה in step 4
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different disqualifier, זמן, treats a partial problem like a full one. Comparing ערלה to זמן would give the opposite result, so the first comparison is not clearly correct.

steps.title: Deciding the comparison: ערלה matches טומאה, not זמן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא decides to compare ערלה to טומאה, because neither applies to all offerings, while זמן applies to every offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see which it is similar to. We derive a matter that does not apply to all offerings from a matter that does not apply to all offerings. Let זמן, which applies to all offerings, not serve as proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tries to settle the dispute between the two comparisons. It picks טומאה for now, because ערלה and טומאה share a key feature that זמן does not have. The next step challenges this choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערלה rule applies only to the פסח. The rule that טומאה blocks someone's offering also does not apply everywhere, since for other offerings an impure person can have a messenger bring it for him. זמן applies to every offering, so it is a weaker match, and ערלה follows טומאה: one ערל does not ruin the offering for the group.

keyTerms.meaning: let us see which it resembles

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's first choice is to compare ערלה to טומאה, because both apply only to some offerings. This choice is not final: the next step offers a rival comparison, and the ברייתא ends up deciding through the verse ״זאת״. רבה's proof comes from that verse, not from this comparison.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows the ברייתא's method: two disqualifiers can each serve as a model, and each one points to a different result. Because logic can be argued in both directions here, the ברייתא will need a verse to decide.

phrases.english: Let us see to which it is similar:
we derive a matter that does not apply
to all offerings
from a matter that does not apply
to all offerings,
and let time-intent not serve as proof,
which applies to all offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rival comparison of step 5 and goes back to the טומאה comparison of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picking the closer comparison based on a shared feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ערלה might be like זמן, so a partial ערלה would ruin the whole offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tentatively, ערלה is like טומאה, since both apply only to some offerings, so a partial ערלה would not ruin the offering for the group. The next step challenges this.

steps.title: The ברייתא flips the comparison: ערלה is more like זמן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proposes a new reason to compare ערלה to זמן instead of טומאה. ערלה and זמן never have exceptions, while טומאה sometimes does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe go this way: we compare a rule that never has an exception (ערלה) to another rule that never has an exception (מחשבת זמן). And don't bring proof from טומאה, because טומאה does have an exception.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back against its own decision from Step 6. It offers a new similarity that links ערלה to זמן, which would mean that even a partial ערלה ruins the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6 the ברייתא matched ערלה with טומאה because neither applies to every offering. Now it finds a stronger match the other way. טומאה is sometimes allowed, for example when most of the community is טמא (טומאה דחויה בציבור). Being an ערל and intending to eat after the allowed time are never allowed. Logic alone cannot decide, so step 8 turns to a verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Go this way, a formula for offering a competing line of reasoning
We derive or compare (one law from another)
Was permitted from its general rule, meaning it has an exception
Prove; here, serve as the model for comparison

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'טומאה was permitted from its rule' does not mean טומאה is not a real disqualification. It means that in special cases, such as when the community is mostly טמא, the קרבן פסח may be brought anyway.

phrases.english: Or go this way:
We derive a matter that was never permitted from its rule (ערלה)
from a matter that was never permitted from its rule (זמן)
phrases.notes: Neither ערלה nor improper intent about time ever has an exception.

phrases.english: and let טומאה not serve as proof
since it was permitted from its rule.
phrases.notes: טומאה is set aside when the community is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the decision in Step 6 by proposing a stronger link between ערלה and זמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion of Step 6 that ערלה should be compared to טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ערלה and זמן share the feature of having no exceptions, while טומאה has one. So ערלה should follow זמן, and even a partial ערלה would disqualify.

steps.title: The verse ״זאת״ settles the question
steps.stepSummary: Since logic can point either way, the ברייתא turns to a verse: ״זאת״.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends the back-and-forth by quoting a word from the פסוק. This line sets up the next move, because the גמרא will now ask what exactly ״זאת״ teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two logical comparisons cancel each other out, the ברייתא relies on a verse instead of reasoning. The word ״זאת״ comes from ״זאת חקת הפסח״, and it implies a limitation. Steps 9-10 explain what it limits.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; introduces a scriptural source that decides the issue
"This"; a word that limits or excludes

phrases.english: The verse states: "This."
phrases.notes: The word ״זאת״ comes from ״זאת חקת הפסח״ (שמות יב:מג).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the deadlock between the two comparisons in Steps 6 and 7 by citing a verse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Logic might lead us to compare ערלה to זמן, so that a partial ערלה disqualifies.
steps.terutzMaskana: A verse, ״זאת״, decides the matter. Its exact meaning is clarified next.

steps.title: The גמרא asks what ״זאת״ adds, since ״וכל ערל״ already teaches the partial rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the simple reading of ״זאת״. If it only teaches that a partial ערלה does not disqualify, that is already known from ״וכל ערל״.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does ״זאת״ teach? If you say it teaches that when all are ערלים the offering is disqualified, but when only some are it is not, that is already learned from ״וכל ערל״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now speaks in its own voice. It asks what ״זאת״ teaches and rejects the obvious answer, because that answer would make ״זאת״ unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״כל״ ("all") in ״וכל ערל לא יאכל בו״ already shows that the offering is disqualified only when all the intended eaters are ערלים. So ״זאת״ must teach something new. This sets up the real reading in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
Part of it, meaning only some of the group

phrases.english: What does "this" teach?
If you say: when all are uncircumcised, it disqualifies,
when only part are, it does not disqualify,
that is already derived from "and all uncircumcised"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the verse cited in Step 8 actually teaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading that ״זאת״ teaches the partial-ערלה rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That rule already comes from ״וכל ערל״, so ״זאת״ would be redundant. A verse is not redundant.

steps.title: ״וכל ערל״ teaches the partial rule; ״זאת״ limits the disqualification to שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. ״וכל ערל״ teaches that only a fully ערל group disqualifies. ״זאת״ teaches that this applies only at שחיטה, and at זריקה even a fully ערל group does not disqualify. This proves רבה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what the ברייתא means: the verse says ״וכל ערל״, so if all are ערלים it disqualifies, and if only some are, it does not. And if you say the same applies to זריקה, that a fully ערל group at least disqualifies, the verse says ״זאת״: only at שחיטה does a fully ערל group disqualify, but at זריקה, even if all are ערלים, it does not disqualify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא so that each verse teaches something different. This gives רבה the proof he promised in Step 3: intent for ערלים at the זריקה does not ruin the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא really holds two separate rules. ״וכל ערל״ covers how many ערלים there must be (all of them, not just some). ״זאת״ covers when the intent counts (only at שחיטה, not at זריקה). That second rule is exactly the question from Step 2, and it is decided in favor of רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that; introduces the correct reading

steps.whatToRemember: In רבה's reading, ״וכל ערל״ means only a fully ערל group disqualifies, and ״זאת״ means this applies only at שחיטה. So at זריקה, intent for ערלים never disqualifies. רב חסדא reads the same ברייתא the opposite way, and רב אשי later rejects both readings.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes רבה's ראיה from Step 3 and answers the question from Step 2: intent for ערלים is not effective at the זריקה.

phrases.english: Rather, is this not what it teaches:
The verse states "and all uncircumcised":
if all are uncircumcised, it disqualifies;
if only part are, it does not disqualify.
And if you say the same applies to sprinkling,
that if all are uncircumcised it at least disqualifies,
the verse states "this":

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁחִיטָה הוּא דְּכוּלַּהּ עׇרְלָה מִיהָא פָּסְלָה,
phrases.english: it is at slaughter that a fully uncircumcised group disqualifies,
but at sprinkling,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ כּוּלַּהּ עׇרְלָה נָמֵי לָא פָּסְלָה.
phrases.english: even if all are uncircumcised, it does not disqualify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9 by giving each verse a separate role, which also proves רבה's position.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the verses: each word teaches a different rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״זאת″ seemed to repeat the partial-ערלה rule already taught by ״וכל ערל״.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״זאת״ limits the disqualification to שחיטה. At זריקה, even a fully ערל group does not disqualify.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's view that intent for ערלים at the זריקה is ineffective

steps.title: Why is זריקה more lenient than שחיטה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes זריקה different, so that intent for ערלים does not disqualify there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you ask: what is the leniency of זריקה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא anticipates a natural question: why should שחיטה and זריקה be treated differently? This line sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In many areas of קדשים, intent at זריקה counts just like intent at שחיטה. So a reason is needed for why this kind of intent is ignored at זריקה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say or ask

phrases.english: And if you ask: what is the leniency of sprinkling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the שחיטה/זריקה distinction drawn in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason intent for ערלים does not disqualify at זריקה

steps.title: Intent about who will eat does not apply at זריקה
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that מחשבת אוכלין, intent concerning who will eat the offering, has no effect at the זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because intent about the eaters does not apply at זריקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the leniency. Intent for ערלים is a type of intent about the eaters, and that type only matters at שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Intending to feed the offering to ערלים is a form of מחשבת אוכלין. This category of intent works only at שחיטה, so at זריקה it has no effect at all. That explains why ״זאת״ limits the disqualification to שחיטה, as רבה holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Intent concerning who will eat the offering
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, מחשבת אוכלין, including intent for ערלים, matters only at שחיטה and not at זריקה.

phrases.english: Because there is no intent regarding eaters at sprinkling.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מחשבת אוכלין has no effect at the זריקה, so intent for ערלים there does not disqualify.

steps.title: רב חסדא reads ״וכל ערל״ the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא reverses the reading. ״וכל ערל״ teaches that at שחיטה only a fully ערל group disqualifies, but at זריקה even a partly ערל group disqualifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא says the opposite. The verse says ״וכל ערל״. If all of the group is ערל, the offering is disqualified. If only part of it is ערל, it is not disqualified. But at the זריקה, even part of the group being ערל also disqualifies.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא takes the same ברייתא that seemed to prove רבה and flips it around to support his own view. For him, זריקה is the stricter stage, not the more lenient one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both readings agree that ״וכל ערל״ means a fully ערל group. They disagree about what is true at the זריקה. רבה said that at זריקה even a fully ערל group does not disqualify. רב חסדא says the reverse: at זריקה even a partly ערל group disqualifies.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary, the other way around
Part of it (only some members of the group)

steps.confusionAlert: רבה and רב חסדא both say זריקה is different from שחיטה, but in opposite directions. For רבה, זריקה is more lenient: nothing disqualifies there. For רב חסדא, זריקה is stricter: even a partly ערל group disqualifies.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda: on the contrary, the other way around:
phrases.notes: He reads the same ברייתא in the reverse direction.

phrases.english: The verse says, "and all uncircumcised":
if the whole group is uncircumcised, it disqualifies;
if only part of it is, it does not disqualify.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל זְרִיקָה — אֲפִילּוּ מִקְצָתָהּ נָמֵי פָּסְלָה.
phrases.english: But at the sprinkling, even part of the group also disqualifies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a reverse reading of the ברייתא that step 10 had used to prove רבה's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא in the opposite direction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to prove רבה, that זריקה is lenient.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא can be read so that זריקה is stricter, which supports רב חסדא.

steps.title: רב חסדא explains why ״זאת״ is needed
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think זריקה also needs a fully ערל group. ״זאת״ limits the lenient rule to שחיטה, so at זריקה even part of the group disqualifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say the same rule applies to זריקה, so that it does not disqualify unless the whole group is ערל, the verse says ״זאת״. Only at שחיטה does part of the group not disqualify. But at זריקה, even part of the group disqualifies.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא heads off a possible objection: maybe the 'whole group' rule also applies to זריקה. He answers that the word ״זאת״ limits that rule to שחיטה alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״זאת״ is a limiting word: 'this', and nothing else. For רבה, it limited the disqualification to שחיטה. For רב חסדא, it limits the leniency to שחיטה. So the same word serves both sides, depending on what you think it is limiting.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible objection)

phrases.english: And if you would say the same applies to the sprinkling,

phrases.aramaic: דְּעַד דְּאִיכָּא כּוּלַּהּ עׇרְלָה לָא פָּסְלָה,
phrases.english: that it does not disqualify unless the whole group is uncircumcised,
the verse says "this":
it is only at slaughter that part of the group does not disqualify,
but at the sprinkling even part of the group disqualifies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's reading by explaining the role of ״זאת״.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting word (מיעוט) applied to the leniency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps זריקה, like שחיטה, needs a fully ערל group.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״זאת״ limits the leniency to שחיטה, so at זריקה even part of the group disqualifies.

steps.title: Why should זריקה be stricter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why זריקה would be stricter than שחיטה according to רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would ask: what is the special strictness of זריקה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רב חסדא's reading. Why should זריקה be more sensitive to wrong intent than שחיטה? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question mirrors step 11, which asked why זריקה was more lenient according to רבה. Now each view must explain why it treats זריקה differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: And if you would ask: what is the stringency of the sprinkling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the logic behind רב חסדא's stricter view of זריקה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes זריקה stricter than שחיטה regarding intent for ערלים.

steps.title: פיגול becomes fixed only at זריקה
steps.stepSummary: זריקה is stricter because an offering's status as פיגול is only finally set at the זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because פיגול is fixed only at the זריקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that זריקה is the stage where the offering's status is finally decided. So wrong intent there carries extra weight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offering becomes פיגול through wrong intent about the time it will be eaten. That status is confirmed only when the זריקה, the last essential service, is done. Since זריקה is the deciding moment for intent, רב חסדא treats it as the most sensitive stage, even for a partly ערל group.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering ruined by intent to eat it after its allowed time

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two opposite pictures of זריקה. For רבה, intent about who eats has no effect at זריקה. For רב חסדא, זריקה is the key moment for intent.

phrases.english: For פיגול is established only at the sprinkling.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זריקה is the stage that finally fixes פיגול, so intent there is most powerful.

steps.title: רב אשי: maybe ״וכל ערל״ means even one
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges both readings. Perhaps ״וכל ערל״ means even one ערל, and ״זאת״ teaches that we need the whole group, at both שחיטה and זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenged this: how do you know ״וכל ערל״ means all of them? Maybe ״וכל ערל״ means any ערל at all. Then the Torah wrote ״זאת״ to teach that it does not disqualify unless the whole group is ערל, with no difference between שחיטה and זריקה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the starting point that both רבה and רב חסדא share. He offers another reading of the ברייתא in which ״זאת״ makes no difference between שחיטה and זריקה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both earlier readings assumed ״וכל ערל״ already means 'the whole group', so ״זאת״ was free to teach something about זריקה. רב אשי says ״כל״ may mean 'any', which would disqualify even a partly ערל group. Then ״זאת״ is needed just to require the whole group, at every stage. If so, the ברייתא cannot settle the dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even a little

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not reject the law itself. He only rejects the claim that this ברייתא proves either רבה or רב חסדא.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi strongly challenged this:
From where do you know that "and all uncircumcised" means the whole group?

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא הַאי ״וְכׇל עָרֵל״ מַשְׁמַע כׇּל דְּהוּ עׇרְלָה,
phrases.english: Perhaps "and all uncircumcised" means any uncircumcised at all,
so the Torah wrote "this",

phrases.aramaic: דְּעַד דְּאִיכָּא כּוּלַּהּ עׇרְלָה — לָא פָּסְלָה,
phrases.english: to teach that unless the whole group is uncircumcised, it does not disqualify,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא בִּשְׁחִיטָה וְלָא שְׁנָא בִּזְרִיקָה.
phrases.english: with no difference between slaughter and sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undermines the shared assumption behind both readings of the ברייתא (steps 10 and 13-14).
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that ״וכל ערל״ already means a fully ערל group.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״כל״ means 'any', then ״זאת״ is used up teaching the 'whole group' requirement, and nothing is left to teach a difference for זריקה.

steps.title: רב אשי begins a new explanation of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי starts to give his own explanation of what רב חסדא and רבה argue about. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: רב חסדא and רבה...
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the ברייתא as proof, רב אשי starts a new explanation of the dispute. This line sets up the next move, and its content continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that the earlier approach is dropped. The dispute between רבה and רב חסדא will now be based on a different idea than the reading of ״וכל ערל״ and ״זאת״.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Rav Chisda and Rabba...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the ברייתא-based proof, רב אשי opens a new explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduction to רב אשי's own explanation of the dispute between רבה and רב חסדא (continued on the next amud).
